glossary.AGL: Africa Global Logistics, MSC's port arm
glossary.AMTI: Asia Maritime Transparency Initiative, a CSIS project
glossary.CAMC: China CAMC Engineering, a state firm
glossary.CAMCE: China CAMC Engineering, a state firm
glossary.CGM: CMA CGM, a French shipping line
glossary.CMA: CMA CGM, a French shipping line
glossary.CIC: China Investment Corporation, a sovereign fund
glossary.CNODC: China National Oil and Gas Exploration and Development, a CNPC unit
glossary.COMPLANT: China National Complete Plant Import and Export, a state builder
glossary.COSCO: COSCO Shipping, China's state shipping line
glossary.CSIS: Center for Strategic and International Studies, a US think tank
glossary.HBIS: HBIS, a Chinese state steel group
glossary.HHLA: Hamburger Hafen und Logistik, Hamburg's port operator
glossary.HKND: HKND Group, a Hong Kong company owned by Wang Jing
glossary.ICBC: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China
glossary.INSS: Institute for National Security Studies, an Israeli think tank
glossary.JISCO: Jiuquan Iron and Steel, a Chinese state group
glossary.KCIC: Kereta Cepat Indonesia China, the Jakarta-Bandung rail company
glossary.NORINCO: China North Industries, a state arms and engineering group
glossary.NRTC: National Radio and Telecommunication Corporation of Pakistan
glossary.PLA: People's Liberation Army, China's armed forces
glossary.RTB: RTB Bor, a Serbian copper company
glossary.UDG: Union Development Group, a Chinese developer
glossary.YLB: Yacimientos de Litio Bolivianos, Bolivia's state lithium firm
glossary.AD Ports: Abu Dhabi Ports, the emirate's state port group
glossary.CK: CK Hutchison, a Hong Kong conglomerate
glossary.CLTC: China Satellite Launch and Tracking Control General, a PLA space-tracking unit
glossary.COPHC: China Overseas Port Holding Company, a state firm
glossary.CPFL: CPFL Energia, a Brazilian power company
glossary.ENR: Engineering News-Record, a construction trade journal
glossary.GEDI: Gezhouba Group's power engineering and design arm
glossary.HAPCO: Huajin Aramco Petrochemical Company, a Saudi-Chinese refinery venture
glossary.JEMSE: Jujuy Energía y Minería, the Argentine province of Jujuy's state mining company
glossary.MAPNA: MAPNA Group, an Iranian state engineering firm
glossary.NI 43-101: a Canadian standard for mining technical reports

whats_new.text: Panama took back the two canal ports run by Hong Kong's CK Hutchison after its Supreme Court voided the contract
Guyana opened the new Demerara River Bridge, built by China Railway Construction
Cuba opened the first of 92 solar parks built with Chinese equipment, as China replaces Russia as its main helper
Nicaragua revoked the never-built canal concession of the Hong Kong company HKND

entries.name: Mombasa-Nairobi Standard Gauge Railway
entries.value: $3.2bn; 2014 loans of $1.6bn concessional and $1.63bn commercial
entries.backer: China Exim Bank (about 90%); China Road and Bridge Corp built and operated it
entries.china_gets: Building and operating contracts for a Chinese state firm; Libor+3.6% on the commercial loan; a 15-year take-or-pay cargo guarantee
entries.host_case: Kenya's biggest project since independence; Ruto published the loan documents in 2022

entries.name: Addis Ababa-Djibouti Railway
entries.value: About $4bn; Ethiopia's $2.49bn China Exim loan was restructured in 2018 and now matures in 2044
entries.backer: China Exim Bank; CREC and CCECC built it
entries.china_gets: Building contracts for CREC, CCECC and NORINCO; Libor+3% interest; a supply corridor to Djibouti's ports, where China Merchants owns a stake
entries.host_case: Ethiopia's main route to the sea

entries.name: Port de Djibouti / Doraleh stake
entries.value: China Merchants bought 23.5% of Port de Djibouti S.A. for $185m in 2012-13
entries.backer: China Merchants Port Holdings
entries.china_gets: A share in Djibouti's port operator, on the Bab el-Mandeb strait
entries.host_case: Djibouti presents itself as a neutral hub that hosts many countries' bases

entries.name: PLA support base, Djibouti
entries.value: Opened 1 Aug 2017; lease reported at about $20m a year
entries.backer: People's Liberation Army Navy
entries.china_gets: China's first overseas base; about 400 PLA marines and a pier for large warships (US DoD, cited by CRS)
entries.host_case: Beijing calls it a support facility for anti-piracy and evacuation missions

entries.name: Lamu Port (LAPSSET)
entries.value: First 3 berths; berth 1 opened 20 May 2021
entries.backer: Built by China Communications Construction Co; funded by Kenya
entries.china_gets: A building contract for CCCC; no Chinese ownership stake found
entries.host_case: Kenya's gateway to South Sudan and Ethiopia

entries.name: Bagamoyo Port
entries.value: $10bn plan agreed in 2013 with China Merchants and Oman; suspended in 2019; the Chinese partner pulled out in 2022
entries.backer: Formerly China Merchants; now an MoU with AGL (MSC), signed Dec 2025
entries.china_gets: Nothing; the talks collapsed
entries.host_case: Tanzania's ports authority rejected the terms: tax exemptions and the investors' freedom to set port charges

entries.name: Sicomines copper-cobalt (minerals for infrastructure)
entries.value: Up to $7bn of infrastructure under the revised 2024 deal
entries.backer: Sinohydro and China Railway Group
entries.china_gets: Copper and cobalt output in exchange for infrastructure
entries.host_case: Kinshasa renegotiated the deal for more infrastructure

entries.name: Chinese loans to Africa, 2000-2024
entries.value: $180.87bn in 1,319 loan commitments from 42 lenders (amounts committed, not paid out)
entries.backer: China Exim Bank, China Development Bank and others
entries.china_gets: Interest; contracts for Chinese firms; repayment in resources in some deals
entries.host_case: Governments say they borrowed to fill gaps Western lenders left

entries.name: Top Chinese borrowers in Africa, 2000-2023
entries.value: Angola $46.05bn cumulative; ranking after it: Ethiopia, Egypt, Nigeria, Kenya, Zambia, South Africa, Sudan, Ghana, Cameroon (dollar figures for those not in the brief)
entries.backer: China Exim Bank, China Development Bank
entries.china_gets: Oil-backed repayment in Angola's case; contracts for Chinese firms
entries.host_case: Angola negotiated debt relief in 2024 rather than restructuring

entries.name: Lekki Deep Sea Port
entries.value: Opened 23 Jan 2023
entries.backer: China Harbour Engineering (CHEC) built it; China Development Bank financed
entries.china_gets: CHEC 52.5% stake (Tolaram 22.5%, Lagos 20%, NPA 5%)
entries.host_case: Lagos calls it Nigeria's first deep-sea port

entries.name: Dar es Salaam port upgrade
entries.value: World Bank-financed berths 1-7, RoRo, channel works
entries.backer: China Harbour Engineering (contractor); World Bank financing
entries.china_gets: Construction contracts only; operators are DP World (berths 4-7) and Adani (CT2)
entries.host_case: Dar es Salaam chose Gulf and Indian operators

entries.name: Kribi deep-water port
entries.value: Container terminal run by KCT consortium
entries.backer: China Harbour Engineering built it; CHEC is a KCT shareholder with CMA CGM and Bollore
entries.china_gets: Shareholding in the terminal operator (exact % not confirmed in a filing)
entries.host_case: Cameroon's main deep-water port

entries.name: Husab and Rossing uranium
entries.value: Husab 5,318 t U3O8 (2023); Rossing 68.62% CNUC
entries.backer: CGN and China-Africa Development Fund (Taurus Minerals, 90% of Swakop Uranium); CNNC's CNUC at Rossing
entries.china_gets: Uranium supply; Namibia's state Epangelo holds 10% of Husab
entries.host_case: Namibia keeps a state stake and royalty

entries.name: Arcadia and Bikita lithium
entries.value: Huayou paid $422m for 100% of Arcadia (completed Apr 2022); Sinomine paid $180m for 74% of Bikita
entries.backer: Zhejiang Huayou Cobalt; Sinomine Resource
entries.china_gets: Lithium concentrate for Chinese battery supply chains
entries.host_case: Zimbabwe banned raw lithium ore exports in Dec 2022 to force local processing

entries.name: Gwadar Port (CPEC)
entries.value: 40-year concession held by China Overseas Port Holding Co since 2013
entries.backer: China Overseas Port Holding Co (COPHC)
entries.china_gets: 91% of gross port revenue and 85% of free-zone revenue for 40 years (minister to Senate); an Arabian Sea port near Hormuz
entries.host_case: Pakistan says the port is CPEC's flagship gateway and will return to the Gwadar Port Authority at the end of the concession
entries.confidence_reason: Revenue split stated by Pakistan's minister in the Senate and reported by Dawn

entries.name: CPEC power plants (Chinese IPPs)
entries.value: $15.36bn of outstanding Chinese IPP debt across 21 projects (May 2024); Rs423bn of unpaid dues to Chinese plants (2025); AidData puts the energy portfolio at nearly $20bn
entries.backer: Chinese state-owned and private power companies; Chinese banks
entries.china_gets: Dollar-indexed, government-guaranteed returns on equity; building contracts; debt service
entries.host_case: Pakistan says the plants ended its blackouts and is now trying to stretch out the debt and cut payments
entries.confidence_reason: Figures come from Pakistani press and AidData and cover the whole portfolio; point is the country centroid

entries.name: Hambantota Port
entries.value: $1.12bn deal (2017): $973.66m for 85% of HIPG; 99-year lease
entries.backer: China Merchants Port Holdings; port originally built with Chinese loans
entries.china_gets: Majority control of the port operator for 99 years; a 15-year ban on competing ports within 100 km
entries.host_case: Sri Lanka used the proceeds to ease its debt and kept security oversight; the deal was signed despite opposition objections
entries.confidence_reason: Terms appear in a primary HKEX filing and Reuters reporting

entries.name: Colombo Port City
entries.value: About $1.4bn of CHEC investment; 116 ha of reclaimed land on a 99-year lease
entries.backer: CHEC Port City Colombo (a CCCC subsidiary)
entries.china_gets: Leasehold rights over 116 ha of new land next to the CBD, which it can sublease
entries.host_case: Sri Lanka passed the 2021 Port City Economic Commission Act to create a special financial zone
entries.confidence_reason: Figures come from secondary sources (ISAS NUS, Daily Mirror); the investor's own FAQ confirms the lease structure

entries.name: Padma Bridge Rail Link
entries.value: $2.67bn China Exim preferential buyer's credit (2018) covering 85% of a $3.13bn contract; 2% interest, 20-year term
entries.backer: China Exim Bank; China Railway Group (CREC) built it
entries.china_gets: A large building contract for CREC; interest
entries.host_case: Bangladesh says it is a key link between Dhaka and the southwest
entries.confidence_reason: Loan recorded by AidData and Bangladeshi press

entries.name: Pokhara International Airport
entries.value: China Exim concessional loan of RMB 1.02bn (about $216m), 2% interest
entries.backer: China Exim Bank; China CAMC Engineering
entries.china_gets: Building contract for CAMC; interest
entries.host_case: Nepal asked China to turn the loan into a grant; its anti-graft body charged CAMC and Nepali officials with inflating costs (2025)
entries.confidence_reason: AidData record plus Kathmandu Post and NYT reporting

entries.name: China-Maldives Friendship (Sinamale) Bridge
entries.value: China Exim concessional loan of RMB 455.6m; the bridge cost about $200m
entries.backer: China Exim Bank; CCCC
entries.china_gets: Interest; building contract; influence in Malé
entries.host_case: The 2018 government vowed to renegotiate Chinese debt; Reuters estimated Chinese-linked liabilities at about $1.5bn in 2018
entries.confidence_reason: Loan is documented, but estimates of total Maldives debt to China vary widely

entries.name: Kyaukphyu Deep Sea Port and SEZ
entries.value: Phase 1 cut to $1.3bn in the 2018 framework agreement (from a $7.2bn plan); CITIC holds 70%
entries.backer: CITIC-led consortium
entries.china_gets: Control of a Bay of Bengal port and the pipeline terminus, bypassing Malacca
entries.host_case: Myanmar negotiated CITIC's share down from 85% to 70% and shrank phase 1 over debt-trap fears; the port sits in a conflict zone
entries.confidence_reason: Deal terms are well sourced, but construction status since 2021 is unclear

entries.name: Myanmar-China oil and gas pipelines
entries.value: Oil line design capacity is 22m tonnes a year; gas line 12 bcm a year
entries.backer: CNPC (50.9% of the oil line) with MOGE
entries.china_gets: An energy import route from the Indian Ocean to Yunnan that bypasses Malacca
entries.host_case: Myanmar receives transit fees and gas offtake
entries.confidence_reason: Sourced to a BRI Monitor case study; coordinates mark the Kyaukphyu/Made Island terminus

entries.name: Laos-China Railway (Vientiane-Boten)
entries.value: About $5.9-6bn line; China holds 70% of the JV; about 60% debt-financed
entries.backer: Chinese state firms (JV); Chinese lenders
entries.china_gets: Rail link from Kunming toward Thailand and Singapore; JV control
entries.host_case: Laos calls it the way to turn a landlocked country into a land-linked one; economists warn about debt
entries.confidence_reason: Reuters and AP

entries.name: Ream Naval Base expansion
entries.value: China funded a 300m deep-water pier, a 5,000-ton dry dock and a joint logistics and training centre (opened Apr 2025)
entries.backer: Chinese government (PLA)
entries.china_gets: PLAN corvettes have berthed continuously at the main pier since Dec 2023 (AMTI); joint training centre on the Gulf of Thailand
entries.host_case: Cambodia says the base is open to all friendly navies; a US warship docked there in 2026
entries.confidence_reason: Construction and use are documented, but whether China has exclusive access is contested

entries.name: Dara Sakor (UDG) development
entries.value: 99-year land lease (2008)
entries.backer: Tianjin Union Development Group (UDG)
entries.china_gets: Coastal land and a long runway that the US says could host military assets
entries.host_case: Cambodia calls it a tourism project; the US sanctioned UDG in 2020 over evictions and corruption
entries.confidence_reason: The military use claim is US government allegation and analysts dispute it; the sanction itself is documented

entries.name: Jakarta-Bandung High-Speed Railway (Whoosh)
entries.value: $7.3bn including a $1.2bn overrun; 75% financed by China Development Bank (2% on USD, 3.46% on CNY); restructuring talks in 2025
entries.backer: China Development Bank; Chinese consortium holds 40% of KCIC
entries.china_gets: Interest; equity in the operator
entries.host_case: Prabowo pledged state support; Indonesian SOEs are absorbing the losses; the anti-graft agency (KPK) is investigating possible mark-ups
entries.confidence_reason: Straits Times and The Diplomat

entries.name: Indonesia Morowali Industrial Park (IMIP)
entries.value: CDB loans for the park's power stations include $384m for phase 1 and a $559-574m share of a syndicated loan for phase 3
entries.backer: Tsingshan Group with Bintang Delapan; China Development Bank
entries.china_gets: Nickel supply for stainless steel and EV batteries; operating control
entries.host_case: Indonesia's nickel export ban was meant to force processing onshore
entries.confidence_reason: AidData records plus the park's own site

entries.name: East Coast Rail Link (ECRL)
entries.value: Construction cost RM50.27bn; RM74.96bn including development costs
entries.backer: China Communications Construction Co (CCCC)
entries.china_gets: Building contract; a land bridge that offers a Malacca alternative
entries.host_case: Malaysia renegotiated the cost down in 2019; the line is due to open Jan 2027
entries.confidence_reason: Malaysian transport ministry figures reported by The Edge

entries.name: Thai-Chinese HSR (Bangkok-Nakhon Ratchasima)
entries.value: 179.412bn baht for phase 1; Thailand pays for construction
entries.backer: Thailand funds it; China supplies technical systems
entries.china_gets: Technical systems contracts; a link to the Laos-China railway
entries.host_case: Thailand chose to self-finance; the project is behind schedule, with service targeted for 2030
entries.confidence_reason: Thai project site and Reuters; no Chinese loan

entries.name: Cat Linh-Ha Dong Metro, Hanoi
entries.value: Cost rose 57% to $868m; China Exim loans of about $670m
entries.backer: China Exim Bank
entries.china_gets: Interest; building contract
entries.host_case: Vietnam criticised delays and overruns; auditors flagged improper costs
entries.confidence_reason: AidData record plus Vietnamese press

entries.name: New Centennial Water Source-Kaliwa Dam
entries.value: $211.2m China Exim preferential buyer's credit (2018); 2% interest, 20-year term
entries.backer: China Exim Bank
entries.china_gets: Interest; building contract
entries.host_case: Manila says the dam is needed for its water supply
entries.confidence_reason: Loan agreement published by the Philippine Department of Finance

entries.name: Chancay Port
entries.value: $1.3bn first phase; COSCO bought 60% of Terminales Portuarios Chancay for $225m in 2019
entries.backer: COSCO Shipping Ports (60%); Volcan (40%)
entries.china_gets: Majority control of a deep-water Pacific hub with 1m TEU capacity and direct Shanghai routes; the terminal owns its land, so no concession is needed
entries.host_case: Peru says Chancay will make it a regional trade hub and cut shipping time to China by 12 days; US officials have raised possible military use
entries.confidence_reason: Stake and price in COSCO's own exchange filing; cost and inauguration confirmed by Peru's state news agency and Reuters

entries.name: Espacio Lejano deep-space station (Neuquén)
entries.value: 200-hectare site on a 50-year tax-free lease; China funded about $54.5m of construction (House Select Committee figure)
entries.backer: China Satellite Launch and Tracking Control General (CLTC, PLA-linked); China Harbour Engineering built it
entries.china_gets: A 35m deep-space antenna in the southern hemisphere for tracking, command and data, run under Chinese labour law with no effective Argentine inspection
entries.host_case: Argentina says the station is civilian (a 2016 addendum says so) and compares it to the ESA station in Mendoza
entries.confidence_reason: The lease and PLA-linked operator are well documented; military use is alleged, not proven

entries.name: Coca Codo Sinclair hydroelectric plant
entries.value: $1.98bn EPC contract; $1.68bn China Exim loan at 6.9% (85% of cost); Ecuador's comptroller found 7,648 cracks
entries.backer: China Exim Bank; Sinohydro (PowerChina) built it
entries.china_gets: The building contract, a 6.9% fixed-rate loan insured by Sinosure; in the 2025 settlement PowerChina takes over operation
entries.host_case: Ecuador's largest power plant (1,500 MW); Ecuador went to ICC arbitration over defects, then in 2025 agreed to drop it
entries.confidence_reason: Loan terms from AidData's project record; defects from Ecuador's Contraloría; settlement reported by Reuters

entries.name: CDB oil-backed loans and PetroChina prepayments
entries.value: Several CDB facilities, e.g. $2.05bn (2011, repaid early in 2018) and $2.03bn (2016); PetroChina $1bn oil prepayment
entries.backer: China Development Bank; PetroChina / Unipec
entries.china_gets: Repayment from Petroecuador oil sales routed into CDB-controlled accounts with minimum balances; long-term crude supply
entries.host_case: Ecuador says the loans financed infrastructure and has prepaid or rescheduled them, with maturities extended to 2027
entries.confidence_reason: Loan facilities and repayment mechanics documented in AidData project records

entries.name: Joint China-Venezuela Fund (oil-for-loans)
entries.value: $60bn+ CDB commitments via the Joint Fund since 2007; AidData counts $105.6bn of Chinese loan commitments 2000-2018; $10-15bn estimated outstanding (2026)
entries.backer: China Development Bank; CNPC/ChinaOil buys the oil
entries.china_gets: Oil cargoes for debt service, paid into a CDB collection account with set-off rights
entries.host_case: Venezuela defaulted in 2017; China granted grace periods; US control of exports in 2026 caught cargoes that had been servicing Chinese debt
entries.confidence_reason: Structure and totals from AidData; current outstanding range from Reuters citing SocGen and JPMorgan (estimates differ)

entries.name: Uyuni lithium plants (YLB-CBC)
entries.value: $1.03bn contract for two direct-extraction plants, 35,000 t/yr lithium carbonate
entries.backer: Hong Kong CBC consortium (includes CATL); state YLB holds 51%
entries.china_gets: Building and operating rights at the world's largest lithium resource, at CBC's own cost and risk
entries.host_case: Bolivia's government backs the deal; a court suspended its passage in 2025 pending environmental studies and indigenous consultation
entries.confidence_reason: Contract signed and reported by Reuters and Bolivia's energy ministry, but not ratified and no plant is operating

entries.name: Tianqi stake in SQM (Salar de Atacama)
entries.value: About 22% of SQM held by Tianqi Lithium
entries.backer: Tianqi Lithium
entries.china_gets: A large minority stake in the world's second-biggest lithium producer and a share of its Atacama brine output
entries.host_case: Chile put Atacama lithium under a Codelco-SQM partnership; Tianqi's legal challenge was rejected by the Supreme Court in January 2026
entries.confidence_reason: Stake and the court ruling reported by Chile's state defence council and Caixin

entries.name: Cauchari-Olaroz lithium
entries.value: 40,000 t/yr lithium carbonate; production began June 2023
entries.backer: Ganfeng Lithium (with Lithium Argentina and Jujuy's JEMSE)
entries.china_gets: Lithium carbonate supply for Chinese battery makers
entries.host_case: Jujuy province is a partner through JEMSE and backs lithium output as a source of revenue
entries.confidence_reason: Start-up reported by market and Chinese business press; ownership shares not set out in these sources

entries.name: Mariana lithium
entries.value: 20,000 t/yr lithium chloride first phase; production began February 2025
entries.backer: Ganfeng Lithium
entries.china_gets: Lithium chloride feedstock for Ganfeng's refineries
entries.host_case: Salta province promotes the project as investment and jobs
entries.confidence_reason: Start-up in Ganfeng's exchange filing and Reuters; no investment figure in these sources

entries.name: Tres Quebradas (3Q) lithium
entries.value: 20,000 t/yr lithium carbonate first phase; production began September 2025
entries.backer: Zijin Mining
entries.china_gets: Lithium carbonate supply
entries.host_case: Catamarca province backs the project as investment
entries.confidence_reason: Start-up reported only by the company; site could not be reached for verification

entries.name: Néstor Kirchner and Jorge Cepernic dams (Santa Cruz)
entries.value: $4.71bn syndicated loan (CDB $2.49bn, ICBC, Bank of China), signed 2014; works largely stalled since 2023
entries.backer: China Development Bank, ICBC, Bank of China; Gezhouba-led consortium builds
entries.china_gets: The building contract and loan repayment; the deal was tied to the wider China-Argentina strategic partnership
entries.host_case: Argentina says the 1,310 MW dams are needed for power; successive governments renegotiated and delayed them
entries.confidence_reason: Loan in AidData's record and Argentina's Boletín Oficial; stalled status from Argentine press

entries.name: Belgrano Cargas freight railway rehabilitation
entries.value: $2.47bn CMEC contract (2010); $2.1bn CDB/ICBC buyer's credit (2012) covering 85%
entries.backer: China Development Bank, ICBC; China Machinery Engineering Corp (CMEC)
entries.china_gets: The rehabilitation contract, Chinese rolling stock and rail supplies, and a freight route for northern grain to the ports
entries.host_case: Argentina says the line cuts the cost of moving grain from the north to the river ports
entries.confidence_reason: Contract and loan documented in AidData and Argentina's official contract text

entries.name: China-Argentina currency swap
entries.value: $18bn swap line; the activated CNY35bn (about $5bn) tranche was renewed in April 2025
entries.backer: People's Bank of China
entries.china_gets: Wider use of the yuan in Argentina's reserves and trade and political leverage over a reserve-poor central bank
entries.host_case: Argentina's central bank says the swap supports its reserves; the US has urged Argentina to end it
entries.confidence_reason: Central bank statement and Reuters

entries.name: TCP container terminal, Paranaguá
entries.value: R$2.9bn (about $924m) for 90% of TCP; deal closed February 2018
entries.backer: China Merchants Port Holdings
entries.china_gets: Control of Brazil's third-largest container terminal, a main outlet for grain and meat exports
entries.host_case: Brazil's transport ministry welcomed the investment
entries.confidence_reason: Price and stake in CMPort's exchange filing and Brazil's transport ministry

entries.name: State Grid Brazil: Belo Monte lines and CPFL Energia
entries.value: Two ±800 kV Belo Monte UHV lines (won 2014 and 2015); 54.6% of CPFL Energia bought in 2017, later about 84%
entries.backer: State Grid Corporation of China (State Grid Brazil Holding)
entries.china_gets: Ownership of long-distance transmission and Brazil's largest private distributor; a showcase for Chinese UHV technology
entries.host_case: Brazil awarded the lines at public auction and approved the CPFL purchase
entries.confidence_reason: Auctions from Brazil's mines and energy ministry; history from State Grid Brazil

entries.name: CNOOC stake in the Stabroek Block
entries.value: 25% working interest (ExxonMobil 45% operator; Hess/Chevron 30%); the block passed 500m barrels produced in 2024
entries.backer: CNOOC
entries.china_gets: A quarter of the consortium's oil from one of the world's fastest-growing fields
entries.host_case: Guyana says its share of the oil is rising as cost recovery falls
entries.confidence_reason: Ownership shares widely reported, including by Guyana's own information department

entries.name: Bogotá Metro Line 1
entries.value: COP13.83 trillion concession (about $3.55bn, Reuters); 23.96km elevated line, 16 stations
entries.backer: China Harbour Engineering (85%) and Xi'an Rail Transportation Group (15%) as Metro Línea 1
entries.china_gets: A 28-year concession to build, supply trains for and run the line for 20 years
entries.host_case: Colombia's government and Bogotá signed it as the city's first metro
entries.confidence_reason: Concession terms from Colombia's transport ministry and Bogotá city hall

entries.name: Mirador copper mine
entries.value: $329m CDB-backed loan to buy Corriente Resources (2010); $1.29bn syndicated loan for mine development (2014); exports began 2019
entries.backer: CRCC-Tongguan (China Railway Construction Corp and Tongling Nonferrous) via EcuaCorriente; China Development Bank
entries.china_gets: Ecuador's first large-scale copper mine and its concentrate
entries.host_case: Ecuador's government signed an addendum to expand output; local and indigenous groups contest its impact
entries.confidence_reason: Loans in AidData records; first exports reported by Reuters

entries.name: Las Bambas copper mine
entries.value: $5.85bn purchase from Glencore (2014) by an MMG-led Chinese consortium; MMG announced a $2bn investment in 2022
entries.backer: MMG (China Minmetals), Guoxin, CITIC
entries.china_gets: One of the world's biggest copper mines and its concentrate
entries.host_case: Peru counts on the mine for revenue; communities have blocked the mining road repeatedly over land and compensation
entries.confidence_reason: Price from CITIC; conflicts and investment reported by Reuters

entries.name: Khorgos Gateway dry port
entries.value: 49% bought in 2017 (24.5% each); COSCO paid about $38m for its share
entries.backer: COSCO Shipping and Lianyungang Port; KTZ (Kazakh railways) keeps 51%
entries.china_gets: A minority stake in the main rail transfer hub on the China-Europe overland route, linked to Lianyungang's sea-rail service
entries.host_case: Kazakhstan says the deal brings Khorgos into COSCO's global logistics network and makes it a regional hub
entries.confidence_reason: Stakes and the deal confirmed by Kazakh state news agency and company filings as reported by port.today

entries.name: Central Asia-China gas pipeline, Lines A-C
entries.value: Three parallel lines of about 1,830km each; 55 bcm/yr combined (A and B 15 bcm each, C 25 bcm); opened 2009-2014
entries.backer: CNPC with Turkmen, Uzbek and Kazakh state gas companies
entries.china_gets: About a fifth of China's gas use from Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan, by an overland route that avoids sea lanes
entries.host_case: Transit states earn fees and an export outlet; Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan have cut exports to meet winter demand at home
entries.confidence_reason: Capacities from a peer-reviewed Nature Communications table and S&P Global

entries.name: Central Asia-China gas pipeline, Line D
entries.value: 966km, 30 bcm/yr planned; Tajik section needs 42 tunnels (63.3km); Tajikistan expects more than $3bn of Chinese investment
entries.backer: CNPC (Trans-Asia Gas Pipeline Co) with Tajiktransgaz, Uzbekneftegaz and Kyrgyz partners
entries.china_gets: A shorter route for gas from Turkmenistan's Galkynysh field
entries.host_case: Tajikistan says its section is settled and blames price disputes between other countries; construction has been halted since the 2014 groundbreaking
entries.confidence_reason: Groundbreaking documented; current status reported only through Tajik minister's statements and an unnamed S&P source

entries.name: Kazakhstan-China oil pipeline (Atasu-Alashankou)

entries.backer: Chinese government
entries.china_gets: Access to research on one of the world's largest nodule fields
entries.host_case: The Cook Islands says it protects its interests; New Zealand objected to not being consulted and paused funding
entries.confidence_reason: The agreement is signed and public, but no projects have been delivered yet

entries.name: Fiji-China police cooperation agreement
entries.value: 2011 memorandum kept after a 2024 review, but Chinese officers embedded in Fiji's police were sent home; Fijian officers still train in China
entries.backer: Chinese Ministry of Public Security
entries.china_gets: A policing foothold in a key Pacific state
entries.host_case: Rabuka's government narrowed it but did not cancel it
entries.confidence_reason: The review outcome was reported by the Guardian, ABC and FBC

entries.name: Balboa and Cristóbal container ports (Panama Ports Company)
entries.value: Run since 1997 by Panama Ports Company, a CK Hutchison unit; extended in 2021 to 2047; the 2025 sale to a BlackRock and MSC group (part of a $22.8bn, 43-port deal) stalled when COSCO sought a stake; Panama's Supreme Court voided the contract on 29 Jan 2026 and the state took the ports in Feb 2026
entries.backer: CK Hutchison (Hong Kong conglomerate); COSCO Shipping sought a stake in the 2025 sale
entries.china_gets: Until 2026, a Hong Kong group's control of the container terminals at both ends of the Panama Canal; in the 2025 sale talks Beijing pressed for COSCO, a Chinese state shipping line, to get a share
entries.host_case: Panama's comptroller found unpaid fees and a 2021 extension that was never approved; the court ruled the deal unconstitutional and Maersk now runs the ports on an interim basis; Hutchison denies wrongdoing
entries.confidence_reason: The operator is a private Hong Kong company, not a Chinese state firm; the court ruling and seizure are documented

entries.name: Fourth bridge over the Panama Canal
entries.value: $1.42bn design-and-build contract awarded in 2018; road and metro-rail crossing
entries.backer: Panama Cuarto Puente consortium of China Communications Construction (CCCC) and China Harbour Engineering (CHEC), both Chinese state firms
entries.china_gets: A flagship construction contract on the canal itself for Chinese state builders
entries.host_case: Panama says the bridge relieves traffic between Panama City and the western suburbs and carries Metro Line 3
entries.confidence_reason: The award is documented; later delays and changes to the timetable are not fully confirmed in the sources

entries.name: Panama City-David railway (cancelled)
entries.value: Chinese feasibility study delivered in March 2019: 391km, about $4.1bn; shelved by the Cortizo government in September 2019
entries.backer: China Railway Design Corporation (study, paid for by China)
entries.china_gets: Would have been a large railway-building contract; nothing was built
entries.host_case: President Varela backed it after Panama recognised Beijing in 2017; his successor Cortizo dropped it
entries.confidence_reason: Study and cancellation reported by Panamanian media

entries.name: North-South Highway (Edward Seaga Highway)
entries.value: About $730m; 66km toll road opened 2016; China Development Bank loans of $425.5m plus RMB 200m (Libor+4.6%, 20 years)
entries.backer: China Harbour Engineering (CHEC) through its project company; China Development Bank
entries.china_gets: A 50-year toll concession and the right to up to 1,200 acres of state land along the route
entries.host_case: Jamaica gave no loan or traffic guarantees and says the road cut the Kingston-Ocho Rios trip to under an hour; tolls are criticised as high
entries.confidence_reason: Terms from Jamaica's government information service and AidData

entries.name: Alpart alumina refinery and bauxite lands
entries.value: Bought from Rusal for $299m in 2016, helped by a $170m China Development Bank loan
entries.backer: JISCO (Jiuquan Iron and Steel, a Chinese state steel and aluminium group)
entries.china_gets: A bauxite and alumina source for Chinese aluminium production
entries.host_case: Jamaica welcomed the restart of an idle plant and jobs in the south-west
entries.confidence_reason: Sale confirmed by Rusal; loan by AidData

entries.name: Route 32 widening, San José to Limón
entries.value: $296m China Exim loan signed in 2013 (4%, 20 years); the loan ran out in April 2025 and Costa Rica is finishing the work itself
entries.backer: China Exim Bank; China Harbour Engineering (CHEC) builds it
entries.china_gets: A building contract on the road to Costa Rica's main Caribbean port
entries.host_case: Costa Rica says the road is vital for exports through Limón; delays and cost overruns are a domestic issue
entries.confidence_reason: Loan terms from AidData and Costa Rica's public works ministry

entries.name: National Stadium, San José
entries.value: About $105m Chinese grant; opened 2011
entries.backer: Chinese government grant; built by a Chinese state firm
entries.china_gets: A visible reward after Costa Rica switched recognition from Taiwan to Beijing in 2007
entries.host_case: Costa Rica got a national stadium at no cost
entries.confidence_reason: Grant recorded by AidData

entries.name: Moín oil refinery joint venture (cancelled)
entries.value: $1.3bn upgrade planned through Soresco, a 50-50 venture of state oil firm Recope and CNPC; halted in 2013 and cancelled in 2016
entries.backer: CNPC (China National Petroleum Corporation) and China Development Bank financing
entries.china_gets: Would have given a Chinese state oil firm half of Costa Rica's only refinery; nothing was built
entries.host_case: Costa Rica's comptroller found a conflict of interest because the feasibility study was done by a CNPC subsidiary
entries.confidence_reason: Halt and cancellation reported by Reuters and the Tico Times

entries.name: Baha Mar resort, Nassau
entries.value: $2.45bn China Exim loan (2010; Libor+3.9%); bankruptcy in 2015; sold by the bank's holding vehicle to Hong Kong's Chow Tai Fook Enterprises in 2017
entries.backer: China Exim Bank; China State Construction Engineering (CSCEC) built it and put in $150m
entries.china_gets: Interest income and a huge contract for a Chinese state builder; the bank took control of the resort after the collapse
entries.host_case: The Bahamas backed the project as a jobs engine; the developer blamed the Chinese builder for delays
entries.confidence_reason: Loan terms from AidData and the loan documents; the sale reported by PR Newswire and the Tribune

entries.name: North Abaco port
entries.value: About $40m China Exim loan (2%, 20 years) for the port and a bridge; handed over in 2018
entries.backer: China Exim Bank; China Harbour Engineering (CHEC) built it
entries.china_gets: A building contract about 200 miles from Florida; no Chinese operating rights
entries.host_case: The Bahamas wanted a second port for Abaco; it is still mostly unused for commercial shipping
entries.confidence_reason: Loan and contract announced by the Bahamas government; use reported by the Tribune

entries.name: Suspected Chinese-linked listening stations (Bejucal and El Salao)
entries.value: No figures; satellite images show active antennas at Bejucal near Havana and a large antenna ring under construction at El Salao near Guantanamo since 2021; work at El Salao stopped by April 2025
entries.backer: Cuban military with suspected Chinese involvement (reported)
entries.china_gets: Possible electronic eavesdropping on US military and space activity in the south-eastern US
entries.host_case: Cuba and China deny any Chinese spy base
entries.confidence_reason: Based on CSIS satellite analysis and anonymous US officials; China's role is not confirmed

entries.name: Santiago de Cuba multipurpose terminal
entries.value: $120m China Exim loan; built 2015-2018, opened January 2019
entries.backer: China Exim Bank; China Communications Construction (CCCC)
entries.china_gets: A building contract and a creditor role in Cuba's second port
entries.host_case: Cuba says the terminal modernises trade for the east of the island
entries.confidence_reason: Loan recorded by AidData; opening reported by Cuban media

entries.name: Chinese-supplied solar parks
entries.value: 92 parks planned, 55 in 2025, aiming at more than 2,000 megawatts by 2028; China donated equipment for 22 parks (120 megawatts) in 2025
entries.backer: Chinese state equipment makers, including Shanghai Electric; Chinese government donation
entries.china_gets: Influence as Cuba's main helper in its power crisis, taking Russia's place
entries.host_case: Cuba says the parks are its fastest way to end blackouts
entries.confidence_reason: Reported by Reuters with figures from Cuba's energy ministry

entries.name: St John's deep-water harbour
entries.value: About $90m; RMB 600m China Exim concessional loan (2%, matures 2038); finished 2020
entries.backer: China Exim Bank; China Civil Engineering Construction (CCECC)
entries.china_gets: A building contract and creditor role in the main port of a small island state
entries.host_case: Antigua says the port lets bigger cruise and cargo ships call
entries.confidence_reason: Loan terms from AidData; completion reported locally

entries.name: Phoenix Park industrial estate, Point Lisas
entries.value: Opened January 2024; financed by China Exim Bank and built by Beijing Construction Engineering Group (BCEG)
entries.backer: China Exim Bank; BCEG (a Beijing state builder)
entries.china_gets: A Caribbean manufacturing base where Chinese firms lease space
entries.host_case: Trinidad wants the estate to draw manufacturing and diversify from oil and gas
entries.confidence_reason: Opening confirmed by Trinidad's trade ministry; loan size not published

entries.name: Sam Lord's Castle hotel
entries.value: $170m China Exim buyer's credit; opened as a Wyndham Grand hotel in October 2023
entries.backer: China Exim Bank; COMPLANT (a Chinese state builder) built it
entries.china_gets: A building contract and interest income
entries.host_case: Barbados backed the rebuilt resort for tourism jobs; local builders complained of being pushed out
entries.confidence_reason: Loan recorded by AidData; opening by Wyndham

entries.name: New Demerara River Bridge
entries.value: $260.85m contract signed 2022; opened October 2025; paid for by Guyana
entries.backer: China Railway Construction Corporation (CRCC) group
entries.china_gets: A large building contract in a fast-growing oil economy
entries.host_case: Guyana says the four-lane bridge ends chronic traffic on the old floating bridge
entries.confidence_reason: Contract and opening confirmed by Guyana's information department

entries.name: Nicaragua canal concession (revoked)
entries.value: Granted in 2013 to HKND, a Hong Kong company owned by businessman Wang Jing; nothing beyond a symbolic start was built; repealed in May 2024
entries.backer: HKND Group (private, Hong Kong)
entries.china_gets: Would have given a Chinese businessman a 50-year (renewable) right to build a rival to the Panama Canal
entries.host_case: Ortega's government revoked the concession and says it will seek other investors; farmers had protested land seizures
entries.confidence_reason: Repeal published in Nicaragua's official gazette and reported by AP

entries.name: Punta Huete international airport rebuild
entries.value: RMB 2.87bn (about $400m) credit from CAMCE approved in 2024 (15 years, about 5.2%), after Nicaragua switched recognition from Taiwan to Beijing in 2021
entries.backer: China CAMC Engineering (CAMCE), a Chinese state firm, as lender and builder
entries.china_gets: A building contract and creditor role at a former military airfield near Managua
entries.host_case: Nicaragua says the airport will be a new international gateway
entries.confidence_reason: Loan terms in Nicaragua's legislative decree and AidData

entries.name: National Library and La Libertad tourist pier
entries.value: National Library opened November 2023 (about $54m, mostly Chinese); La Libertad pier, about $23m Chinese grant, opened 2024
entries.backer: Chinese government grants
entries.china_gets: Visible goodwill after El Salvador switched recognition from Taiwan to Beijing in 2018
entries.host_case: President Bukele presents both as Chinese gifts with no strings
entries.confidence_reason: Opening reported by AP; pier grant recorded by AidData

entries.name: Patuca III hydropower dam
entries.value: 104 megawatts; opened January 2021; phase 2 financed by a $297.7m ICBC loan
entries.backer: Sinohydro (PowerChina); ICBC (a Chinese state bank)
entries.china_gets: A dam contract won before Honduras switched recognition from Taiwan to Beijing in 2023
entries.host_case: Honduras says the dam cuts reliance on imported fuel for power
entries.confidence_reason: Loan recorded by AidData
